messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: comparison of gibbs sampler & stan; two level random effects model
parts:
Hi,

By accident I compared gibbs sampler with stan (using identical priors) for a two level random effects model and found that stan estimate for between group variation is quite different from gibbs while estimates for within group variation is the same. I have 10 groups (lots) with 12 units (samples) each. Can somebody explain the difference? WinBUGS and stan models are attached as well as estimates (stan density is in red). Data (not simulated) is attached in WinBUGS format.

I appreciate any insight into this. Hopefully neither estimate is biased, I just messed up.

Linas

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] comparison of gibbs sampler & stan; two level random effects model
parts:
Bob,

Actually changing stan code to mu ~ normal (processMean, sigmaB); fixed things. Can you explain why the following code is not equivalent?

   for (n in 1 : N)
      Y [n] ~ normal (mu [lot [n]], sigmaW);
   mu ~ normal (processMean, sigmaB);

and
   for (n in 1 : N)
      Y [n] ~ normal (processMean+sigmaB*iii [lot [n]], sigmaW);
   iii ~ normal (0,1);

Thanks for the insight,
Linas
